original_value: AbstractPublic key encryption With keyword search (PEKS) enables a cloud server (CS) to get the search trapdoor to identify ciphertext containing the target keyword without decrypting the ciphertext or knowing the target keyword. With the advent of mobile cloud computing, PEKS has ushered in an era of new development opportunities and new challenges. In mobile cloud computing environment, the PEKS schemes demand strict bounded timing response and security. However, traditional PEKS schemes rely on heavy bilinear pairing computations, which causes a delay from the CS to the mobile terminal. Moreover, as computing power increases, PEKS is more vulnerable to suffer from an inherent insecurity known as inside keyword guessing attack, which leaks user data query information. To achieve a secure and efficient searchable encryption scheme in the mobile cloud computing environment, we put forward a lattice‐based searchable encryption scheme that supports conjunctive keyword search. Our scheme achieves higher computational efficiency and is resistant against quantum attacks compared with traditional PEKS schemes. To further enhance security and make our scheme secure against keyword guessing attack, we hide the decryption parameters by outsourcing part of the decryption process to a semitrusted third party called unusual keyword server, so that the CS cannot guess the exact keyword by performing consistency verification.

result.paraphrase: AbstractPublic key encryption with keyword search (PEKS) allows a cloud server (CS) to obtain a search trapdoor and identify ciphertexts containing a target keyword without decrypting them or learning the keyword itself. With the rise of mobile cloud computing, PEKS has opened up new development opportunities as well as new challenges. In mobile cloud environments, PEKS schemes require strict bounded response time and security. However, conventional PEKS schemes depend on costly bilinear pairing computations, which introduce delays between the CS and mobile terminals. In addition, as computing power grows, PEKS becomes more susceptible to an inherent weakness called an inside keyword guessing attack, which can expose users’ query information. To build a secure and efficient searchable encryption scheme for the mobile cloud environment, we propose a lattice-based searchable encryption scheme supporting conjunctive keyword search. Compared with traditional PEKS schemes, our scheme offers higher computational efficiency and resistance to quantum attacks. To further strengthen security and defend against keyword guessing attacks, we conceal the decryption parameters by outsourcing part of the decryption process to a semitrusted third party called an unusual keyword server, preventing the CS from inferring the exact keyword through consistency verification.
